snippets.text: The Independent Market Monitor (IMM) has reported on the declining number of shortage pricing intervals in ERCOT, as well as the reduced prices during those intervals.

For example, the IMM noted that the Operating Reserve Demand Curve (ORDC) was active (a level ofat least $0.01 per MWh) for only 57 hours in 2025, which was less than 8% of the annual average for 2021- 2

024, with an average price during those active hours of $2.26/MWh, reflecting the lowest price over the past five years.1 The IMM has recognized that increased capacity in ERCOT at present is mainly due to the growth of solar and batteries, which in turn keeps prices affordable for consumers and have largely outpaced large load additions, helping to bolster grid reliability.

The IMM has also warned about the dangers to the market due to the over-reliance on out- of-market actions: Ideally, markets should procure and dispatch all resources needed to operate the system reliably.
In practice, however, operators often supplement market 1 IMM 2025 State of the Market Report at 8, figure 5.

Before TSSA can offer specific proposed modifications, ERCOT and the IMM should first analytically model pricing outcomes under different designs of the ASDCs to determine the options that best provides robust price signals to minimize out-of-market interventions in the long run and generate sufficient revenues for a new entrant to recover its Cost of New Entry (CONE).
